datasets.title: Atmospheric CO2 at Mauna Loa, monthly
datasets.description: Monthly mean dry-air CO2 mole fraction at Mauna Loa (ppm) and the same with the seasonal cycle removed.
datasets.provider: NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory (GML), with the 1958-1974 record of C. D. Keeling, Scripps Institution of Oceanography
datasets.licence: US Government work, public domain; NOAA asks for credit and a citation (Lan et al., NOAA GML)
datasets.citation: Lan, X., Tans, P. and Thoning, K.W.: Trends in globally-averaged CO2 determined from NOAA Global Monitoring Laboratory measurements.
datasets.version: NOAA GML co2_mm_mlo.csv, file created Sat Sep  5 03:55:38 2026
datasets.missing: No month is empty: NOAA fills the few months without measurements by interpolation (ndays = -1 in its file) and says so in the file header. The deseasonalized column is the provider's own.

datasets.title: GISTEMP v4 surface temperature anomaly: global, northern and southern hemisphere, monthly
datasets.description: Land-ocean temperature index (LOTI), anomalies in degrees C relative to 1951-1980.
datasets.provider: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies (GISS)
datasets.licence: NASA data, public domain; GISS asks to cite GISTEMP Team and Lenssen et al. (2024)
datasets.citation: GISTEMP Team: GISS Surface Temperature Analysis (GISTEMP), version 4. NASA GISS. Lenssen, N. et al. (2024), J. Geophys. Res. Atmos., doi:10.1029/2023JD040179.
datasets.missing: The provider publishes values to 0.01 °C; months not yet analysed are left empty.

datasets.title: HadCRUT5 global temperature anomaly, monthly, with 95 % uncertainty range
datasets.description: Global mean near-surface temperature anomaly (degrees C) relative to 1961-1990, 1850 to now, with the lower and upper 95 % limits.
datasets.provider: Met Office Hadley Centre / Climatic Research Unit, University of East Anglia
datasets.licence: Open Government Licence v3.0 (contains public sector information); cite Morice et al. (2021)
datasets.citation: Morice, C.P. et al. (2021), An updated assessment of near-surface temperature change from 1850: the HadCRUT5 data set, J. Geophys. Res. Atmos., 126, e2019JD032361.
datasets.version: HadCRUT.5.2.0.0, analysis, global monthly summary series

datasets.title: Oceanic Nino Index (ONI), ENSO
datasets.description: 3-month running mean of the Nino 3.4 sea-surface temperature anomaly (degrees C, ERSSTv5, centred 30-year base periods). Each value is placed on the middle month of its 3-month season (DJF = January).
datasets.citation: NOAA CPC: Oceanic Nino Index (ONI), ERSSTv5 Nino 3.4 region, 3-month running mean.
datasets.missing: Each 3-month season is placed on its middle month, so the record ends one month before the latest month observed.

datasets.title: Arctic sea-ice extent, monthly (Sea Ice Index)
datasets.description: Monthly mean Northern Hemisphere sea-ice extent and area, millions of km2, from passive-microwave satellites, November 1978 onwards (two months, December 1987 and January 1988, have no data).
datasets.provider: NOAA@NSIDC, National Snow and Ice Data Center
datasets.licence: Free and open access; citation required as a condition of use (Fetterer et al., doi:10.7265/a98x-0f50)
datasets.citation: Fetterer, F., Knowles, K., Meier, W. N., Savoie, M., Windnagel, A. K. & Stafford, T. Sea Ice Index, Version 4 (G02135). NSIDC. doi:10.7265/a98x-0f50.
datasets.version: Sea Ice Index v4.0 (monthly extent files)

datasets.title: World CO2 emissions per year (fossil fuels, cement, land use)
datasets.description: Annual emissions of the world, million tonnes of CO2 (fossil fuels and cement; including land-use change from 1850), and cumulative totals.
datasets.provider: Our World in Data, from the Global Carbon Project (Global Carbon Budget) and others
datasets.licence: Creative Commons Attribution 4.0 (CC BY 4.0); credit Our World in Data and the Global Carbon Project
datasets.citation: Our World in Data CO2 and Greenhouse Gas Emissions dataset, based on the Global Carbon Budget (Friedlingstein et al.), World rows.

columns.name: Cumulative CO2 emissions (fossil fuels and cement)
Cumulative CO2 emissions including land-use change

datasets.missing: Series start when the provider's estimates start (fossil CO2 1750, oil 1855, gas 1882, cement 1880, land use 1850).

datasets.title: Global mean sea level, tide-gauge reconstruction 1880-2013
datasets.description: Annual global mean sea level in mm (arbitrary zero), with its uncertainty, reconstructed from tide gauges.
datasets.licence: Free to use; the provider asks that the source is acknowledged. The data page states no formal licence
datasets.citation: Church, J.A. and White, N.J. (2011), Sea-level rise from the late 19th to the early 21st century, Surveys in Geophysics, 32, 585-602.
datasets.version: Church and White 2011, update to 2013 (files dated June 2015)

datasets.title: Global mean sea level from satellite altimetry, 1993-now
datasets.description: Global mean sea level anomaly in mm from successive altimetry missions, about every 10 days, annual cycle removed.
datasets.licence: US Government work, public domain; acknowledgment requested: 'Altimetry data are provided by NOAA Laboratory for Satellite Altimetry.'
datasets.citation: NOAA Laboratory for Satellite Altimetry: Sea level rise (TOPEX/Poseidon, Jason-1/2/3, Sentinel-6MF), global ocean 66S to 66N, annual signals removed, no glacial isostatic adjustment.
datasets.note: Provider's own trend of the whole record: 3.17 mm/year (no glacial isostatic adjustment correction).

datasets.title: Stratospheric aerosol optical depth (volcanic forcing) 1850-2012
datasets.description: Monthly global and hemispheric mean stratospheric aerosol optical depth at 550 nm (dimensionless), a measure of volcanic eruptions.
datasets.provider: NASA Goddard Institute for Space Studies (Sato, Lacis, Hansen)
datasets.licence: NASA data, public domain; cite Sato et al. (1993) and the GISS forcing page
datasets.citation: Sato, M., Hansen, J.E., McCormick, M.P. and Pollack, J.B. (1993), Stratospheric aerosol optical depths 1850-1990, J. Geophys. Res., 98, 22987-22994 (extended by GISS to 2012).

not_included: Solar activity (sunspot number): the SILSO series is licensed CC BY-NC (non-commercial), so it is not shipped. The NOAA SWPC F10.7 table starts only in 2004. Import one with File > Import CSV.
Ice-core CO2 before 1958: not downloaded; the model builds the earlier path from cumulative emissions and says so.
